messages:
mei: heads-up — onboarding polaris-lite-v1 (int8) showed a reproducible quality dip for zh->en samples with vertical/furigana-style input. baseline fp16 vs int8 delta is bigger than expected.
mei: quick numbers from the smoke suite: baseline fp16 BLEU=29.6, polaris-lite int8 BLEU=25.9 (±0.2), chrF drop too.
mei: example (original vertical-furigana sample):
mei: ```
mei: input: \u300e\u65e5\u672c\u8a9e\u30d5\u30ea\u30ac\u30ca\u300f
mei: reference: "Japanese text (with ruby) explanation."
mei: fp16_out: "Japanese text (with ruby) explanation."
mei: int8_out: "Japanese tex (with ruby) explanation"  <-- missing 't' and punctuation shift, and sometimes fused tokens
mei: ```
arjun: weird, looks like a token boundary/merge issue. did tokenizer change between builds?
mei: checked tokenmaps: model repo uses tokenizer v2.3, our quant pipeline applied the locale-proxy mapping (experimental) that rewrites some ZWSP/ZWJ handling. suspect shadowing at the CJK/latin boundary.
taylor: can you paste the diff of token ids for that phrase? small reproducer would help.
mei: here is a minimal repro command we used on canary containers:
mei: ```
mei: ./eval_run --model polaris-lite-v1:int8 --batch 1 --lang zh-en --dataset vertical-furigana-small --metrics bleu,chrF --save-batches /tmp/pol-lite/batches
mei: ```
mei: infra-bot: canary deploy 2026-03-20T14:22:10 finished (polaris-lite-v1:int8) — nodes: canary-03 (g5), canary-04 (a10). logs: /mnt/artifacts/4987654321/canary.log
mei: I attached the token id sequence for the problematic sentence into artifact (see link below).
mei: eval-bot: artifacts uploaded: https://artifacts.redwood.ai/4987654321/pol-lite-int8-repro.tar.gz
lina: grabbing sample now. quick grep shows U+200B (ZWSP) insertion before Latin runs in pretokenized input. we strip it earlier, but locale-proxy added a normalization rule mapping NBSP->ZWSP as part of an experiment.
arjun: ah — that mapping would change byte offsets and maybe change BPE merges, causing the kernel quant paths to hit different attention patterns. could produce off-by-one merges in decoder.
taylor: action: run tokenizer diff and kernel-bisect on the quantized runtime. i'll kick off a bisect script that toggles the locale-proxy normalization.
taylor: bisect command (running):
	`bash infra/scripts/quant_bisect.sh --model polaris-lite-v1 --variant int8 --toggle-norm locale-proxy --cases 200`
mei: also attaching deterministic pair of outputs (fp16 vs int8) for the sample ids: 0042, 0043, 0099.
mei: quick manual inspection: when ZWSP present, fp16 splits tokens as [KANJI][ZWSP][latin] -> good; int8 path sometimes collapses ZWSP+latin into single subword and drops punctuation alignment.
lina: uploading tokenmaps and v2.3 tokenizer graph: /mnt/artifacts/4987654321/tokenmaps/
arjun: if the kernel selection heuristic depends on sequence length modulo block size, a tiny change in tokenization can flip which GEMM/kernels used. that could explain quality swing if one kernel had a precision artifact under quantization.
mei: ok, plan: (1) taylor to finish bisect and report which kernel path flips; (2) l1 to re-run small eval with locale-proxy disabled to confirm regression disappears; (3) arjun to add targeted unit test for ZWSP+latin boundaries.
	taylor: started bisect job 4987654338, ETA ~35m. logging to same artifact bucket.
	lina: re-run with locale-proxy OFF now (job 4987654345) — preliminary BLEU=29.4 on same smoke set.
mei: great — disabling locale-proxy seems to recover most of the delta. this narrows root cause to normalization rule.
arjun: if confirmed, we should revert mapping in the quant pipeline and add a guard that prevents locale-proxy from applying to models flagged as "do-not-normalize-cjk-latin" during onboarding.
mei: assigning follow-ups: @taylor add bisect results to the PR, @lina rollback mapping in quant pipeline for canary, @arjun add unit tests and a comment in onboarding checklist.
mei: thanks everyone. I'll open a short postmortem after we nail the repro and fix. :thumbsup:
